stem.text: Let \( g(x) = \int_{x^{2}}^{x} \frac{1}{t} \, dt \). Find the exact value of \( g'\left(2\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Split the integral at any constant k in the domain of the integrand: \( g(x) = \int_{k}^{x} \frac{1}{t} \, dt - \int_{k}^{x^{2}} \frac{1}{t} \, dt \), and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to each piece.
With the chain rule, \( g'(x) = f\left(x\right) \cdot 1 - f\left(x^{2}\right) \cdot 2 x \).
At \( x = 2 \): the limits are \( 2 \) and \( 4 \), with derivatives \( 1 \) and \( 4 \), and \( f\left(2\right) = \frac{1}{2} \), \( f\left(4\right) = \frac{1}{4} \).
